newsitem.title: CANADA: Chauvco says deal proves interest in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Chauvco says deal proves interest in Canada.

text.p: Chauvco Resources Ltd, with its C$55 million acquisition of Tidal Resources Inc, hopes to convince investors that western Canadian operations remain a major focus for the company, Chauvco chief financial officer Jim Wilson said on Tuesday.

"In '97 it looks like we could be spending an increased budget on our properties in western Canada," Wilson said in an interview. "We're balancing some of the projects against our international operations, but I think this does show the market our continuing interest in western Canada."

Chauvco, which has for the past few years received more attention for its operations in Argentina, said earlier it struck a deal to acquire Tidal for C$2.05 per share in cash for a total of C$45 million plus Tidal's debt.
The target firm comes with estimated proven plus probable reserves of 4.5 million barrels of oil and 39 billion cubic feet of gas.
Wilson said Tidal's Chinchaga property in northwestern Alberta made a good fit with its own core area there.
The purchase also gives Chauvco a new foothold in North Dakota, he said.
He said the company, which earlier this year signed a deal to explore Gabon, continued to examine several countries in hopes of forging a major new operating area to complement Argentina.
"It does take a while to find suitable international projects. We've told the market that we'll be looking for other opportunities internationally and we're doing that," Wilson said.
He declined to give the geographical regions Chauvco was concentrating on but said the firm had "a lot of irons in the fore."
